text: Filippo Monteforte/AFP/Getty Images Vatican says the 71-year-old pontiff is recovering at a Rome hospital after a ‘successful’ surgery What to know about pulmonary adenocarcinoma Pulmonary adenocarcinoma, which accounts for about 40% of all lung cancer cases, usually grows and spreads more slowly than some other kinds of lung cancer. • Video 1:07 Video 1:07 Video Here are the details on Pope’s cancer procedure 1:07 Pope Leo XIV had surgery at Agostino Gemelli University Policlinic in northwest Rome to remove a nodule that was determined to be pulmonary adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer. The Vatican said surgeons removed the cancerous growth, along with the lower lobe of his right lung.
